item.title: Keeneland Race Course hosts top thoroughbred horses in Breeders' Cup
item.description: One of the most exciting moments of 2026 is here for the sport of thoroughbred horse racing. The Breeders’ Cup World Championships , which brings together elite horses, jockeys, trainers, and owners from around the world, returns to the historic Keeneland Race Course in Lexington, Kentucky, for the annual two-day international series of Grade 1 thoroughbred races on Friday, Oct. 30 and Saturday, Oct. 31. The Breeders’ Cup will feature 14 championship Grade 1 races, with $34 million in purses and awards up for grabs, attracting the top talent in the sport. The competition for U.S. Horse of the Year honors is full of talented horses. Forever Young, the Japanese sensation and reigning Breeders’ Cup Classic champion, seeks to defend his title. He will face stiff competition from last year’s Horse of the Year, Sovereignty, and from Golden Tempo, the winner of both the 2026 Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes. These contenders, along with several other accomplished horses, are competing for the title. Here’s a look at what you need to know ahead of the 2026 Breeders’ Cup, taking place at Keeneland. item.title: Mikel Arteta defends reaction to Max Dowman red card: ‘This is not Disneyland’
item.description: Mikel Arteta has defended his reaction to Max Dowman ’s red card against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday and has launched a scathing criticism of the 16-year-old’s three-match ban, claiming he could have broken his foot as a result of the challenge that led to his controversial sending off. Arteta appeared to be angry with the teenager as he made his way off the pitch following his red card, which followed a dangerous tackle from behind from Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal in the 85th minute of the shock defeat in the Carabao Cup. Arteta has issued a warning to the 16-year-old Dowman (Getty) Arteta had suggested after the loss to the League Two side that he warned Dowman to be ready for heavy challenges and had urged him not to react to physical treatment, and issued a warning to the teenager on Friday that he is not in “Disneyland”. "What do you expect?” Arteta said before Sunday’s match at Liverpool . “That’s the level and that’s the reaction. Whether it’s right or wrong, that’s the reaction. And the reaction when I don’t win, I’m f----- off, big time. This is the environment and the reality. "We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League. We look after him so much but we are also demanding as he needs to earn the right to play otherwise what are the rest of the boys going to tell me? Arsenal failed in their bid to overturn Dowman’s three-game ban with the Football Association confirming they had dismissed claims of both “wrongful dismissal and excessive punishment”. More follows

item.title: Sam Hauser on how Boston Celtics playing differently with Jayson Tatum
item.description: It may yet be early in the Boston Celtics 2026-27 NBA regular season campaign, but there are some clear tendencies that can be seen on the court in how Boston head coach Joe Mazzulla has his team playing. Among them is the uptick in attempts by his teammates to get star Celtics forward Jayson Tatum open off the ball. That has not been lost on vet sharpshooter Sam Hauser, who sees it as part of how the team has adjusted to this version of the team on the court. "I think it's just like we're just playing within the flow of the offense," said Hauser via CLNS Media. "And I think just naturally, he's been able to play a little bit more off-ball and get different looks and score in different ways. That's what makes him really good; he can score at all three levels and then score with the ball and without the ball." "I feel like each and every night we brought really good activity and playmaking," he added, "whether it's deflection, steals, blocks, whatever it may be, charges, drawing a legal screen." "So I think we've done a good job of that," said the Virginia alum. "It was really just trying to clean up communication a little bit." "We're flying around, everybody's trying to make a play, and sometimes when there's no communication, two or three guys are maybe doing the same thing at once, when only one guy can take care of it – little things like that." item.description: Credit: Scott Utterback/Courier Journal The college basketball season officially starts on Nov. 1, so you can expect to see Jay Bilas plenty over the next several months. The ESPN analyst is looking forward to what should be another intriguing year. Florida is ranked No. 1 in both the preseason Associated Press Top 25 and the USA Today Coaches Poll . Duke is No. 2 in both polls. The Blue Devils open their season Monday at home against Army, and Bilas will be on the broadcast. We recently spoke with Bilas about what to expect from the college basketball season. Note: This interview has been edited and condensed for length and clarity. What stands out to you about Duke? Jay Bilas: “Duke’s the most talented team in the country, top to bottom. They have everything. They have size. They have depth, about 10 deep. They can play in multiple ways. They’ve got experience and really good guards. They can shoot it. I think the exhibition games are an indication: beating Kansas at Kansas and then just kind of taking apart Tennessee this month. And look, Florida is going to be an outstanding team and arguably the preseason No. 1. But as we go through the season and Duke plays a really challenging schedule, there’s no team I see that matches them personnel-wise. They’re going to win a lot of games, but that doesn’t mean they’re going to win the whole thing; they certainly have the pieces to do it.” So, if you had a vote, would Duke be your preseason No. 1? “I don’t know who the best team is yet, and I’m not sure we ever do. It’s rare to have a preseason No. 1 and feel comfortable saying they’ll win the whole thing, because you have to win six games in the tournament to win a championship. It’s perhaps not the best way to crown a champion, but it’s an unbelievable spectacle. item.description: Ballston Spa senior Leah Szmarz, center, plays the ball in front of Columbia junior Madelyn Marra and teammate freshman Charlotte Haskell during the Section 2, Class AA semifinals on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026, in Stillwater, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) STILLWATER - Tom Rogan spent more than two decades leading the Bethlehem girls' soccer team to success. Now, as coach of Ballston Spa, he will try to lead his Scotties to a sectional title against his former team. Leah Szmarz scored less than two minutes into the first sudden-victory overtime period on Thursday and fifth-seeded Ballston Spa erased a two-goal halftime deficit to beat top-seeded Columbia 3-2. The Scotties earned a spot in the Class AA girls' final against Bethlehem, the program Rogan helped build before taking over the Scotties two seasons ago. The final is at 7:30 p.m. on Tuesday at Shaker High School. Rogan had watched his old team win its semifinal earlier in the day, knowing it would be waiting for them if his players won theirs. "It was emotional watching them win their game," Rogan said of Bethlehem. "It was a privilege and honor to coach them." Rogan led Bethlehem to 348 wins and nine sectional titles over 25 seasons, coaching alongside his wife, Christine Cochrane, who served as an assistant until becoming the head coach at Guilderland in 2023. A year later, Rogan joined her as an assistant for the Lady Dutch, but shortly after the 2024 season ended, Cochrane died at age 36 after battling breast cancer. After Thursday's win, Rogan got choked up talking about the upcoming sectional final against his former team. "There's three kids there that, my wife, Christine, and I coached together," he said. "I love those kids: Mallory (Maycrink), and June (McCarthy), and Kinley (Logsdon). And, we've had June and Kinley since they were seventh graders and they're awesome kids." Twelve minutes later, junior Madelyn Marra doubled the lead, sending the Blue Devils into halftime up 2-0. But Ballston Spa battled back. With 27 minutes left, the Scotties broke through when Szmarz put her head on a cross from Maeve McLoughlin, trimming Columbia's lead to 2-1. item.title: ‘That’s eight more losses for our conference’: Steve Sarkisian questions SEC’s nine-game schedule
item.description: Sep 12, 2026; Austin, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian looks on before the game against the Ohio State Buckeyes at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Scott Wachter-Imagn Images The Texas Longhorns have already lost two SEC games this season, putting their College Football Playoff hopes on thin ice. And Steve Sarkisian thinks the conference’s schedule isn’t doing its teams any favors. Sarkisian questioned the SEC’s move to a nine-game conference schedule this season, saying that the league’s coaches had reservations about it from the start. He argued that the extra conference game means more injuries and more losses for SEC teams, which could hurt them when the playoff committee compares them to teams from other conferences. Texas’ Rocky Season Texas started the season ranked No. 1, but the Longhorns lost back-to-back games to Oklahoma and Florida by identical 27-24 scores. After the Florida loss, Sarkisian reportedly warned Arch Manning that he would make a change at quarterback if things didn’t improve. The Longhorns bounced back with a 34-27 upset of No. 7 Ole Miss last weekend to improve to 5-2, but the win came at a cost, as star left tackle Trevor Goosby is reportedly out for the season with a knee injury. At 2-2 in SEC play, Texas may need to win out to have a real shot at the playoff. And Sarkisian isn’t the only SEC coach who has taken issue with the nine-game schedule, as LSU’s Lane Kiffin has been vocal about it as well. ‘Eight More Losses’ Sarkisian said that the conference’s coaches weren’t on board with the change when it was made. “The 16 head coaches in our conference, I think we all had some reservations about going to the ninth conference game, for a variety of reasons,” Sarkisian said during his weekly media session, via On3 . The first reason, according to Sarkisian, is the physical toll of playing another SEC game. “That’s one more game of the physical pounding that this league takes its toll on you with, right?” he said. “We’ve all, I mean we’re no different than a lot of the other teams, we’ve all suffered some pretty significant injuries along the way,” he said. Sarkisian also questioned how the playoff committee will treat SEC teams with more losses. “I think the other reservation about the ninth game was that’s eight more losses for our conference,” Sarkisian said. “Any way you slice it, it’s eight more losses.” “So what is it really going to look like when there’s 9-3 SEC teams compared to 10-2 or even 11-1 teams from other conferences? How much value is going to be placed in that,” he added. “I think that’s why we were so adamant about if we’re going to go to nine conference games let’s go to nine when we expand.” It’s worth noting that the Big Ten has played a nine-game conference slate since 2017 and the Big 12 has played one since 2011. item.description: Former Real Madrid official reveals club were offered Lionel Messi in 2001: ‘We didn’t want to sever ties with Barcelona’ Real Madrid had an opportunity to sign Lionel Messi in 2001, before the Argentine superstar established himself at Barcelona, Miguel Angel Portugal, a former club official, has revealed. Portugal, who worked at the Santiago Bernabeu as a player, Castilla coach, scout and technical secretary, made the revelation during an interview with AS ahead of Real Madrid’s meeting with Racing Santander. He recalled that someone close to Messi had offered the teenager to Los Blancos while his professional contract situation at Barcelona remained unresolved. Although the information reached the club and there was some contact, Real Madrid ultimately did not pursue the possibility, with Portugal suggesting that maintaining relations with their rivals was an important consideration. item.title: Former Colts guard Quenton Nelson to make debut on MNF with the Seattle Seahawks
item.description: All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson is preparing to make his Seattle Seahawks debut Monday night against the Chicago Bears, giving the Seahawks an eight-time Pro Bowl and three-time All-Pro presence on their offensive line. But before Nelson takes his first snap in a Seahawks uniform, he has another challenge: moving his life and family from Indianapolis to a place they have never lived. The Seahawks are working to make that transition as easy as possible while getting their new guard ready for primetime. Nelson’s reputation as a dominant interior lineman preceded his arrival in Seattle. When head coach Mike Macdonald was asked what stood out while watching Nelson’s tape, his answer was simple. “Well, they run it left,” Macdonald said. “He’s a guy you want to run behind. I know that.” Wide receiver Cooper Kupp has also seen plenty of Nelson over the years. “I’ve been watching him, you know, just brawl the interior line for years now,” Kupp said. For Nelson, the move means learning a new playbook while simultaneously uprooting his life in Indianapolis. “You gotta learn with moving,” Kupp said. “You’re moving significant others, family out here. Where you going to live at? There is just a lot of that is happening still amongst all of this stuff.” Nelson acknowledged the adjustment but said he has support around him. “It’s completely different, but I’ve got great people around me helping me out,” Nelson said. He also appears to be enjoying his new surroundings. “It’s a beautiful state. A really cool city,” Nelson said. “The nature here is sick.” Nelson said he has been impressed by his new teammates as well, particularly Seattle’s defensive front. “I saw two stud DTs and, I mean, the D-line is just filthy,” Nelson said. “The defensive ends as well.” Macdonald said plenty of people within the Seahawks organization are helping Nelson make the transition. “It’s kind of a 12-as-one thing,” Macdonald said. “Like, hey, it takes a lot of people to make this transition happen.” Nelson said he appreciates how much Seattle wanted to bring him aboard. “I’m honored that, like, this team wanted me,” Nelson said. “That the GM and coaches wanted me here, to add to their already amazing team.” Nelson is expected to start Monday night against Chicago at Lumen Field. The matchup will also feature a familiar opponent for Nelson: The Bears added defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans. Nelson regularly faced Simmons while playing for Indianapolis in the AFC South. Asked about seeing Simmons again, Nelson praised the defensive tackle before joking, “I can’t seem to shake the guy.”

item.title: Man United's Munich air disaster memorial vandalised with items stolen by thieves
item.description: A charity has expressed its sadness after items were stolen from a memorial commemorating the Munich air disaster in Germany. Located at Manchesterplatz, the display honours the 23 victims of the tragedy on 6 February 1958, when a plane bringing Manchester United back from Belgrade crashed following a refuelling stop. Eight United players died in the crash. The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF) said it learned earlier this week that a display case had been vandalised and items stolen. Manchester United offered to fund repairs, but the charity had already arranged to cover the cost. MMMF chair Ifty Ahmed said: "The Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation is deeply saddened by this act of vandalism and theft. "Manchesterplatz is a place of enormous significance to the families of the 23 people who lost their lives as a result of the Munich air disaster, and to Manchester United supporters across the world. Eight United players lost their lives in the 1958 crash (Getty) "We are particularly grateful to our friends in Munich, especially the Red Docs, for their continued care and dedication to this very special place, and for acting so swiftly to repair the damage. "Those responsible may have damaged a display case and stolen treasured items, but they cannot steal our memories, diminish our friendship or destroy the legacy of those we remember. Their memory will endure, and the bond between Manchester and Munich will remain unbreakable." Both Manchester United and Munich Police have been contacted for comment. The disaster led to United having to rebuild their squad under Sir Matt Busby, with the Scot going on to guide the club to their first European Cup triumph 10 years later when they beat Benfica 4-1 after extra time in the 1968 final. United have since won the Champions League twice more in 1999 and 2008 with Sir Alex Ferguson in charge, but they are currently enduring one of the most difficult periods in their recent history. The Red Devils have failed to win any of their last eight matches across all competitions, leading to mounting speculation over Michael Carrick’s future. Carrick remains in charge for now, but badly needs a result as United head to Chelsea for a Premier League clash on Saturday.

Many are questioning how Denny Hamlin can have four wins, finish the regular season as the points leader and still be on the verge of losing the championship to a driver who has built his advantage during the Chase. The format behind that possibility is already a source of division. NASCAR scrapped its elimination-style playoffs after the 2025 season, ending a system that had been in place since 2014. The Championship 4 and its winner-take-all finale were gone. For 2026, NASCAR brought back the Chase but the final 10 races still decides the champion without eliminations. A full-season points system was among the options considered, but it was not adopted. The new format has produced a compelling battle, but it has also brought the old argument back. Hamlin entered the Chase as the top seed after winning four races during the regular season. Larson, who went winless over those first 26 races, has caught fire in the postseason, winning three of the first eight Chase races, including Talladega. He now leads Hamlin by 73 points with two races left. For many fans, the issue is not that Larson might clinch before the finale. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Jack Roslovic is a few seasons removed from a brief — and rather unremarkable — stint with the New York Rangers. General manager Chris Drury acquired the then-27-year-old forward from the Columbus Blue Jackets ahead the 2024 NHL Trade Deadline, seeking a complement to Mika Zibanejad and Chris Kreider on New York’s top line. It didn’t quite pan out that way. Roslovic recorded eight points (three goals, five assists) in 19 regular-season games, and another eight points (two goals, six assists) in 16 postseason games. The Presidents’ Trophy-winning Rangers reached the Eastern Conference Final, but by the end of the series, coach Peter Laviolette demoted Roslovic to the fourth line, while another deadline acquisition, Alex Wennberg , skated alongside Kreider and Zibanejad. The 30-year-old signed a two-year, $8 million contract with the Toronto Maple Leafs in July following a pair of 20-goal seasons with the Carolina Hurricanes and Edmonton Oilers respectively in 2024-25 and 2025-26. Through 15 games this season, he’s among the League’s most pleasant surprises. Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller stapled Roslovic to captain Auston Matthews on Toronto’s top line, leaning into their pre-existing chemistry from their days as linemates with USA Hockey’s national development team. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NASCAR’s decision to turn down a research partnership with Fred Lorenzen’s family has raised uncomfortable questions about the sport’s responsibility toward former drivers. And whether business interests could be part of the reason it wants to keep its distance. The proposal was aimed at studying chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) among former racers, a subject that could bring renewed scrutiny to the dangers drivers faced for decades before modern safety measures became standard. A wider investigation could reveal the long-term consequences of repeated head impacts, raise questions about what NASCAR knew about those risks and put pressure on the organization to do more for retired competitors. NASCAR has not said that financial or reputational concerns influenced its decision. But its refusal to join the initiative, despite the family’s willingness to contribute significant funding, has left fans questioning why the sport does not want to be involved. The controversy comes after the confirmation that Lorenzen, a NASCAR Hall of Famer who died in December 2024, had Stage 3 CTE, being the first driver to be diagnosed with it . His family worked for more than six months to secure NASCAR’s support for research led by Boston University’s CTE Center. The proposal called for NASCAR to contribute up to $1 million annually over three years. The family had already pledged $1 million of its own, and Lorenzen’s son Chris offered to match NASCAR’s contribution. NASCAR declined the offer. NASCAR Explained Its Decision Feb 7, 2025; Charlotte, NC, USA; Former NASCAR HOF Inductee’s Bobby Allison and Fred Lorenzen are honored by Winston Kelly, Executive Director of the NASCAR Hall of Fame, at Charlotte Convention Center Crown Ballroom. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images The sanctioning body pointed to its existing medical partnerships and safety programs, including concussion testing, neurologists at race care centers, helmet improvements and research with Wake Forest University using mouthpiece sensors to measure drivers’ head movements. “Our decision should not be interpreted as a reflection on the importance or value of this work,” NASCAR said . “Rather, it reflects our commitment to continuing this longstanding, medically informed approach to driver health and wellness and to focusing our resources on the research, technologies and safety initiatives we believe can have the greatest impact.” However, the initiatives NASCAR show largely focus on protecting current drivers. The Lorenzen family’s proposal also addressed the generation of racers who competed before HANS devices, SAFER barriers and today’s safety standards were introduced. item.title: Popular and talented - but Grealish is running out of chances
item.description: Jack Grealish was excluded from Everton's squad to face Newcastle United in the Carabao Cup for "a breach of club" discipline [Getty Images] When Jack Grealish breezed back into Everton in his white Lamborghini one hour before the end of this summer's transfer deadline, the excitement among supporters and the player himself was clearly evident. Grealish's previous spell on loan at Everton from Manchester City had been cut short by a serious foot injury, but the 31-year-old had produced enough moments of excitement to make his return to the Finch Farm training base a rare moment of joy amid a miserable summer in the transfer market. When Grealish finally left in the early hours - with the deal done and every autograph signed and every selfie posed for - it was a sort of homecoming for an everyman personality Everton fans had come to regard as one of their own. This was a move with a lot riding on it - for Everton manager David Moyes, who had been left with only 18 senior players after a botched transfer window, and especially for Grealish, whose exile from City at the start of the final year of his contract confirmed his banishment. Now, Grealish's future and Everton's faith in him, has reached a defining moment. Grealish's exclusion from Everton's squad before the Carabao Cup tie at home to Newcastle was publicly described as "a breach of club discipline". Specifically, it was a failure to turn up for training on Monday, leaving the talented maverick - who was Britain's first £100m footballer when he signed for City from Aston Villa in summer 2021 - facing another rebuild in his career. Everton's decision to go public before the game with the reasons for Grealish's absence emphasised the seriousness of his transgression. The fall-out means this now looks increasingly like Grealish's 'now or never' moment, because failure at Everton will surely mark a downward spiral from the top echelons of the Premier League. Everton do not regard this week's misdemeanour as marking the proverbial 'Last Chance Saloon' for Grealish. Moyes does not have enough players at his disposal to make rapid outcasts of potential game-changers. But it increases the pressure on the former England forward to win back the faith of fans who love his obvious enjoyment of life and the magic he has shown he can produce. Moyes will hope it is a harsh lesson learned, because Everton now have even more to play for, given Wembley has suddenly coming into view in the Carabao Cup. BBC Sport believes there have been occasional time-keeping issues with Grealish in the past, but nothing on this scale from a personality regarded as a hard trainer who, in general, keeps himself in good condition. Grealish has held talks with those in authority at Everton, where it is sure to have been made crystal clear there must be no repeat, certainly not under a strict disciplinarian such as Moyes, and he must now attempt to be rehabilitated back into the squad. item.description: Liverpool have dropped out of the race to sign forward for £50m Liverpool Step Back from David Otorbi Move After Valencia Contract Twist Liverpool’s search for a right-sided attacker appears to have hit an early barrier, with Valencia moving swiftly to protect David Otorbi amid growing Premier League interest. According to Tribuna Deportivo , Valencia have activated an extension in Otorbi’s contract, taking his deal through to 2031 and significantly increasing his release clause. That development has changed the picture around a player Liverpool had been monitoring closely as they assessed options on the right wing. The 19-year-old has emerged as one of the more intriguing young forwards in Spain. A right-footed winger who usually starts from the right, Otorbi has built his reputation on speed, direct running and a willingness to attack defenders aggressively. He has made tangible progress with Valencia this season and looked to be entering a key stretch in his development before a thigh injury briefly interrupted his momentum. David Otorbi Price Shift Alters Liverpool Plan The previous structure of the deal made it understandable why Liverpool were attentive. Otorbi’s release clause had been set at €30m, roughly £25m, a figure that represented a calculated market opportunity for a player with age, upside and top-flight exposure. That sort of fee can be justified when a recruitment team believes it is moving early on a talent before the wider market hardens. Photo: IMAGO Now, the equation looks very different. Valencia’s move has reportedly doubled the clause to €60m, around £50m, while also rewarding the player with improved terms. At that valuation, Liverpool’s interest has cooled, with the club seemingly unwilling to proceed on those numbers. Liverpool Right Wing Search Continues This remains a notable area of the squad. Liverpool invested heavily in attacking talent during the last window, bringing in Victor Munoz and Bradley Barcola, but the profile of a natural right-sided option still appears to be under consideration. Otorbi looked like one of several market opportunities rather than a signing the club felt compelled to force through at any cost. That is generally how these situations unfold at elite clubs. Strong interest can be genuine, groundwork can be advanced, and yet one contractual move by the selling club changes the economics enough for the buying side to withdraw. It does not necessarily reflect a negative view of the player, more a judgement on value, timing and squad priorities. item.description: KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia — Defending champion and world No. 4-ranked Miyu Yamashita shot a 6-under 66 Friday to take a two-stroke lead after two rounds of the LPGA Tour’s Maybank Championship . The 2025 Women’s British Open winner had a two-round total of 13-under 131 on the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course. She won last year’s Malaysian tournament after a three-way playoff. “I’ve been playing some really good rounds this year especially,” Yamashita said. “My game is in better shape than last year, so my swing feels really good, too.” Julia Lopez Ramirez birdied three of her final four holes for a 66 and was tied for second with Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, who led by a stroke after the first round. “Try to keep your mind cool and your body hydrated in these conditions,” Lopez Ramirez said of her preparations for the weekend in the usual high humidity in Kuala Lumpur. A Lim Kim had the round of the day, a 64, and was in fourth place, three strokes behind Yamashita. Charley Hull had five birdies in her first six holes to move into the lead, but bogeyed two of her final three holes for a 69 and was tied for fifth, four strokes behind. Haeran Ryu, a major winner this year at the Women’s PGA Championship and at the Evian Championship, withdrew before her first-round tee time Thursday due to a strained finger ligament she suffered while riding in a golf cart during the Wednesday pro-am. She was the highest-ranked player in the tournament in the absence of No. 1 Nelly Korda and No. 2 Jeeno Thitikul. Last week, Yuri Yoshida won the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea , the fourth Japanese player this season to win on the LPGA Tour, joining Yamashita, Shiho Kuwaki and Yuna Nishimura.
